items.title: Recon of pi/llama.cpp mechanisms, W1 trace analysis, and fixed W2 decisions
items.instructions: Nothing in this item changes autopilot/, evals/, the live server or turnstile. (A) Write bench/worker_eval/w2_recon.py (host, gpu:false, timeout_min 30). It writes to bench/results/<YYYY-MM-DD>/worker-eval-w2/recon/: (1) pi.txt: `pi --version`, install path, and verbatim excerpts with file:line from pi's installed dist/docs for: the extension API (every event an extension can handle and what it may return; specifically any event that sees or rewrites the message list or provider payload before a model request, tool_call blocking, tool_result rewriting, session start; and whether registerTool can replace a built-in tool such as edit); built-in read/bash truncation constants and the truncation notice text; compaction trigger, reserveTokens/keepRecentTokens semantics, the summary request's max_tokens and whether thinking is on for it; and the pi-ai openai-completions code that serializes earlier assistant thinking (is it sent back as reasoning_content?). (2) llama.txt: the llama-server binary and `--version` used by the live bonsai-2-27b llama-swap entry (read-only), plus source excerpts with file:line for the per-request reasoning-budget fields (exact names, defaults, behaviour at the budget). (3) packages/: `npm pack --ignore-scripts` of pi-hashline-edit and pi-hashline-context-edit (latest), each into its own new empty directory, unpacked; never npm install; packages/manifest.json with name, version, tarball sha256, registry integrity, license. (4) provenance/: rerun the fixed bench/worker_eval/inspect_historical_arm.py so there are raw-blob hashes (do not edit the old arm file). (5) drift.json: current model sha256 (run.py pinned_model_sha256), bonsai-2-27b llama-swap entry, pi version, sandbox image id and turnstile commit, against the values in the five W1 manifests in bench/results/2026-10-13/worker-eval/bonsai-2026-10-12/; `drift: true` if the model sha, llama-swap entry or pi version differs. (B) Write bench/worker_eval/w2_reasoning_probe.py (gpu:true). Use the same tap/turnstile route and bench key that run.py uses, never :11435 directly. Send three identical requests to bonsai-agent with a prompt that elicits long thinking, max_tokens 4096: no budget; budget 256 plus message; budget 1024 plus message. Save raw responses and tap timings in bench/results/<date>/worker-eval-w2/reasoning-probe/ with result.json. Pass = for each budgeted request, reasoning chars <= (budget+64)*4, the message text appears in the reasoning, and the answer is non-empty. (C) Write bench/worker_eval/w1_traces.py (offline, sandbox). It reads the committed events.jsonl, tap.jsonl and record.json of all 44 W1 attempts and writes trace_analysis.json and trace_analysis.md next to the W1 summary.json, with these keys and the method stated for each: time_split (decode s = sum predicted_ms, prefill s = sum prompt_ms, other = wall minus both; pooled, per attempt, and for the 17 timeouts); reply_tokens (predicted_n p50/p75/p90/max; thinking share per reply = thinking chars / all output chars; estimated reasoning tokens per reply = predicted_n * share, with p50/p75/p90); thinking_resent (for consecutive requests with no compaction between, the change in prompt_tokens vs the previous predicted_n plus new tool-result chars/4: confirm or refute that thinking is resent); prompt_composition_at_pressure (estimated thinking and tool-output shares of the prompt at each compaction start and each context overflow); tool_results (count and size distribution by tool; number over 16 KB or over 400 lines; their share of all tool-result chars); compactions (count, wall duration of each with method, output tokens, share of total wall, and the number of timeouts that happened during a compaction or within 5 min after one); length_stops (for each stopReason=length reply: repetition loop yes/no, where loop = a substring of at least 200 chars repeated at least 3 times in the last 4000 chars, with the excerpt); edit_errors (all 18 messages, bucketed: text not found, multiple matches, other); bash_errors (74, bucketed into the top 10 causes); timeout_tail (for each timeout, what was in flight in the last 5 min: long generation, compaction or tool); turns (distribution). (D) Write bench/worker_eval/W2-decisions.md with one section per candidate: the mechanism (cite recon file:line), the fixed values below, and gate outcomes with the numbers from trace_analysis.json. Think-drop: in the outgoing request only, remove thinking blocks from every assistant message except the last 2 (K=2). Reasoning budget: budget = the smallest power of 2 >= W1 p75 estimated reasoning tokens per reply, clamped to [1024, 8192]; message `\n[Thinking budget reached. Stop thinking and act now with what you have.]\n`. If the probe fails, there is no arm; say why. Session budget: warnings at 12 and 16 min elapsed and at turns 30 and 40; at 17.5 min or turn 45, block every tool except submit_request with a message to call it now (`continue` with a note if unfinished); warnings give elapsed and remaining minutes of the real 20-minute limit. Hashline: choose one package that loads with the installed pi (imports resolve to @earendil-works/* or need only a documented rename), has no network, child-process or outside-cwd file access beyond editing, no runtime deps outside pi, and a license that allows vendoring. Put the review in bench/worker_eval/vendor/REVIEW.md, including whether the package changes read output and its token cost. If none passes, there is no arm. Tool-cap gate: run only if >= 20 W1 tool results exceed 16 KB or 400 lines, or those results are >= 20% of all tool-result chars; if run, cap bash and read results at 16 KB/400 lines with a notice saying where the full output is and how to page it. Compaction gate: run only if compaction time is >= 10% of total W1 wall time, or >= 3 timeouts happened during a compaction or within 5 min after one; if run, set compaction.reserveTokens to 16384 and nothing else, and explain from the recon what this changes. Output 32768: allowed in the combination only if at least one W1 length stop is not a loop; otherwise rejected with evidence. Baseline rerun: yes if and only if drift.json says drift. Deferred, with no arm: smaller items (a planner change that fixed replays can't test; goes to W4) and oh-my-pi (deferred; give the reason). End with the queue order: [baseline rerun if drift], w2-think-drop, w2-reasoning-budget, w2-session-budget, w2-hashline, then the gated arms that passed.
items.acceptance: bench/results/<date>/worker-eval-w2/recon/ contains pi.txt, llama.txt, packages/manifest.json (both packages with sha256 and license), a provenance/ report with raw-blob hashes, and drift.json with a boolean drift field. reasoning-probe/result.json records the three requests and a pass/fail per the stated rule. bench/results/2026-10-13/worker-eval/bonsai-2026-10-12/trace_analysis.json has all ten keys (time_split, reply_tokens, thinking_resent, prompt_composition_at_pressure, tool_results, compactions, length_stops, edit_errors, bash_errors, timeout_tail, turns) with numeric values; edit_errors covers exactly 18 and bash_errors exactly 74 errors. bench/worker_eval/W2-decisions.md covers every candidate, and its values, gate numbers and queue order follow the stated rules and match trace_analysis.json. bench/worker_eval/vendor/REVIEW.md exists. `git diff main -- autopilot/ evals/` is empty.

items.title: Harness support, W2 extensions, arm files, queue/compare tools, smoke run
items.instructions: Before changing run.py, commit bench/worker_eval/fixtures/w1_agent_dir.json: the settings.json, models.json and extensions list that the current run.py builds for bonsai-2026-10-12. Then: (1) Extend arms/schema.json with optional fields: hypothesis (string); extension_config (object, written to <agent>/w2-config.json only when present); settings_overrides (object, deep-merged into settings.json); request_body_extra (object; add only if the recon found no pi hook for the reasoning-budget fields, and implement it in a W2-only relay under bench/worker_eval/, not by editing evals/). Allow extensions entries to be directories, copied recursively to extensions/<basename>/. (2) run.py copies <agent>/w2-ext.jsonl to <attempt>/ext.jsonl when it exists; nothing else in the record format changes. (3) Write extensions in bench/worker_eval/extensions/: drop_old_thinking.ts, reasoning_budget.ts (if a pi hook exists), session_budget.ts, and tool_output_cap.ts (only if its gate passed). Vendor the chosen hashline package under bench/worker_eval/vendor/<pkg>@<version>/ with its LICENSE and a PATCH.diff of any changes. Each extension reads its parameters from w2-config.json and appends one JSON line per action to w2-ext.jsonl (for example {"ext":"drop_old_thinking","removed_blocks":n,"removed_chars":c}). The values are those in W2-decisions.md. (4) Arm files: w2-think-drop, w2-reasoning-budget, w2-session-budget, w2-hashline, plus w2-tool-cap and w2-compact-reserve16k only if their gates passed. Each has a hypothesis (mechanism, expected direction for valid rate, kind-match rate and median wall, and which W1 failure count should drop) and sources, and differs from bonsai-2026-10-12 only in its one mechanism. Do not edit bonsai-2026-10-12.json. (5) bench/worker_eval/w2_queue.json: an ordered list of {arm, out} following W2-decisions.md, with out = bench/results/<YYYY-MM-DD>/worker-eval/<arm>. A baseline rerun, if any, uses arm bonsai-2026-10-12 with a new out dir. (6) bench/worker_eval/run_queue.py --queue FILE --budget-min 145 [--repeat 2] [--only CASE]: runs the first incomplete arm, then the next, in one shared budget, reusing run.py's run_all and resume, and never starts an attempt that doesn't fit. It prints records done/44 per arm. (7) bench/worker_eval/compare.py --baseline DIR [--baseline DIR2] --arm DIR ... --out PREFIX writes PREFIX.json and PREFIX.md. Per arm: valid/44, kind_match/44, kind_match/valid, median wall_s, median turns, replay_kind counts (run/infra/continue/done/stuck/none), flag counts (timeout, context_overflow, output_limit, no request, invalid), tool calls and errors by tool, edit-like error rate (edit plus hashline tools), compaction starts, and from tap.jsonl the per-attempt medians of decode s, prefill s, sum predicted_n, sum uncached prompt_n and max prompt_tokens, plus ext.jsonl action counts. Per arm vs baseline: delta, and a 95% paired bootstrap CI that resamples the 22 cases with both repeats (10000 draws, seed 20261013), for valid, kind-match and median wall. spread S = the baseline's |repeat-1 minus repeat-2| value for that metric, or max(S, |rerun minus W1|) if a rerun exists. beyond_spread = the CI excludes 0 AND |delta| > S. It also warns when model sha256 or llama_swap_entry differ between any manifest and W1. (8) Tests in bench/worker_eval/test_run.py (or a new test_w2.py): the W1 arm builds files identical to the fixture; every w2-*.json validates and has a hypothesis; each w2 arm differs from the baseline only in its mechanism fields; the queue rolls over between arms with a fake attempt; compare.py gives deterministic results on a small fixture. (9) Smoke: write bench/worker_eval/w2_smoke_queue.json with every real arm plus w2-smoke-* variants with exaggerated thresholds wherever the real setting would not fire in a short case (session budget 0.5/1/1.5 min, reasoning budget 256, tool cap 1 KB). Smoke arms are never in w2_queue.json. Run request (gpu:true, timeout_min 60): `python3 bench/worker_eval/run_queue.py --queue bench/worker_eval/w2_smoke_queue.json --repeat 1 --only m1-ngram-spec-replay-r5-144acae8e198 --budget-min 55`, with outs under bench/results/<date>/worker-eval-w2-smoke/. Write smoke.md there: one row per smoke arm with record found, extension load errors (the exact loader error string from recon, grepped in stderr.txt), and mechanism evidence.
items.acceptance: `git diff main -- bench/worker_eval/arms/bonsai-2026-10-12.json autopilot/ evals/` is empty. bench/worker_eval/fixtures/w1_agent_dir.json was committed before the run.py change. `python3 -m pytest bench/worker_eval/` passes, including the tests listed in (8). Arm files match W2-decisions.md (gated arms exist only if their gates passed) and each has a hypothesis. w2_queue.json, run_queue.py and compare.py exist. The vendored hashline dir has LICENSE and PATCH.diff. smoke.md shows, for each smoke arm, a record.json, no extension load error, and the mechanism firing in ext.jsonl: think-drop at least one strip with removed_chars>0; reasoning budget the fields sent, and the budget message inside a thinking block for the 256 variant; session budget warn and block events; hashline its edit tool registered in the session's tool list (toolsAdded) and, if used, a call to it; tool cap at least one truncation.

items.title: Full runs: baseline rerun (if drift), w2-think-drop, w2-reasoning-budget
items.instructions: Submit run requests (gpu:true, timeout_min 150) of `python3 bench/worker_eval/run_queue.py --queue bench/worker_eval/w2_queue.json --repeat 2 --budget-min 145`, repeating until the baseline rerun (only if W2-decisions.md requires it), w2-think-drop and w2-reasoning-budget each have 44 records. If chunks remain in this item, it may continue into w2-session-budget. Once an arm has a real record, never change its arm file, the extensions or vendored code it uses, or its out dir. If a bug needs fixing, make a new arm (for example w2-think-drop-v2) with a new out dir, keep the old results, and explain this in W2-decisions.md. If a chunk stops after three infra errors, report it in the next request; do not delete records. For each finished arm, run `python3 bench/worker_eval/summarize.py <out>` and then `--check <out>`. Then run compare.py with the W1 dir bench/results/2026-10-13/worker-eval/bonsai-2026-10-12 as baseline (plus the rerun if any) for the finished arms, writing bench/results/<date>/worker-eval-w2/compare-a.{json,md}. In compare-a.md, add a short paragraph per arm on mechanism stats: think-drop removed chars per attempt and the change in median uncached prompt_n per request vs baseline (the re-prefill cost); reasoning budget hits per attempt and how output-limit and timeout counts changed. Make no claims inside the spread.
items.acceptance: For each finished arm, results.jsonl has exactly 44 unique (case_id, repeat) records covering the 22 cases with repeats 1 and 2. summary.json and summary.md exist and `summarize.py --check` passes. Every chunk manifest exists, and model sha256 and llama_swap_entry match W1 or the mismatch is in compare-a.md. compare-a.json/md has, per arm, the metrics, deltas, CIs, spread S and the beyond_spread flag defined in compare.py. Arm files and extensions used by finished arms are unchanged since their first record (git log). No change under autopilot/.

items.title: Full runs: remaining single-factor arms and the all-singles comparison
items.instructions: Continue the same queue command until every remaining single-factor arm in w2_queue.json has 44 records: w2-session-budget, w2-hashline, and w2-tool-cap / w2-compact-reserve16k if their gates passed. The same rules apply (no edits after a first record, new arm name for fixes, summarize plus --check per arm). Then write bench/results/<date>/worker-eval-w2/compare-singles.{json,md} covering every single-factor arm, including those from runs-single-a, against the W1 baseline (and the rerun if any). Add mechanism stats: session budget warnings and blocks per attempt, the request kinds produced after a block (count continue separately; it can never match a cloud kind), and timeout count vs W1; hashline edit-like error rate vs W1 18/59, bash call and error counts vs W1 712/74, and the median extra read tokens if the package changes read output; tool cap truncations per attempt and the change in max prompt_tokens; compaction arm compaction starts, compaction wall share and context overflows vs W1. Finish with a ranked table by kind-match rate, ties broken by valid rate and then lower median wall.
items.acceptance: Every single-factor arm in w2_queue.json has 44 unique records, summary.json/md, and a passing `summarize.py --check`. compare-singles.json/md contains all single arms with the compare.py metrics, CIs, spread and beyond_spread, the per-arm mechanism stats listed above, and the ranked table. Any arm superseded by a -v2 is listed with the reason. No change under autopilot/.

items.title: Combination arm, advisor grading of the best arm, recommended configuration
items.instructions: (1) Selection, applied mechanically from compare-singles.json: a single-factor change qualifies if its kind-match delta > 0, or its kind-match delta = 0 and its median wall delta < -60 s, and it has no regression beyond spread on valid, kind-match or median wall. If at least 2 qualify, write arms/w2-combo.json: the union of their extensions, extension_config and settings_overrides; max_output_tokens 32768 only if W2-decisions.md allowed it and think-drop qualifies; a hypothesis. Add it to the queue and run it to 44 records with the same rules. If fewer than 2 qualify, do not run a combination; write the reason in bench/worker_eval/W2-recommendation.md. (2) Write bench/results/<date>/worker-eval-w2/compare-final.{json,md}: every arm vs baseline. (3) The best arm is the one with the highest kind-match rate, ties broken by valid rate and then lower median wall. Grade it as W1 did: `python3 bench/worker_eval/grade.py prepare --out <best arm dir>` (at most 10, deterministic strata), then run requests (gpu:false) for `grade.py grade --out ...` and `grade.py verify --out ...`, then `grade.py finalize --out ...`. Outputs go in <best arm dir>/advisor_grading/. (4) Write bench/worker_eval/W2-recommendation.md: the recommended worker configuration (arm name, extensions and versions, settings); its numbers vs W1 with CIs; what was kept, rejected or not tested and why. Give the remaining gap to the cloud worker: the cloud requests are 44/44 valid and kind-matched by construction, with source advisor verdicts of 15 approve / 7 revise out of 22, vs the arm's rates and its graded approve count; report cloud round wall time only if it can be recovered from committed data, otherwise say so. (5) Write serving/w2-worker-config-proposal.md with the exact changes the user would make to autopilot (config.json, worker_agent_dir(), extension files) to deploy the recommendation. Do not edit anything under autopilot/.
items.acceptance: Either arms/w2-combo.json exists with 44 records, summary and a passing check, or W2-recommendation.md shows the selection rule failing with the numbers. compare-final.json/md covers every arm. The best arm's advisor_grading/ has the sample manifest (<= 10 runs), packets, verbatim grade and verify responses, and advisor_grades.jsonl, and the best arm follows the stated rule from compare-final.json. W2-recommendation.md and serving/w2-worker-config-proposal.md exist and their numbers match compare-final.json. `git diff main -- autopilot/` is empty.

items.title: W2 experiment page and parent page updates
items.instructions: Follow site/AUTHORING.md. Write site/series/local-worker/worker-harness.md. Front matter: layer experiment, series local-worker, title "W2: ...", status done, date (first real chunk), updated (today), a one-line tldr, and a summary of at most 200 words with Question/Method/Result in the W1 style. Sections: question and evidence (link the committed files with GitHub URLs as W1 does); arms table (name, single change, hypothesis, gate result); results table per arm (valid/44, kind/44, kind/valid, median wall, deltas with 95% CI, beyond-spread yes/no), with the spread rule stated; failure-mode table per arm (timeout, context overflow, output limit, no request, invalid, edit-like error rate, bash errors, compactions); mechanism stats; combination; advisor sample (approve/revise/reject, marked as a small judged sample); recommended configuration and the remaining gap to the cloud worker; not tested and why (gated-out arms with their gate numbers, the 32k output decision, smaller items -> W4, oh-my-pi deferred); caveats (N=2 on 22 M1 cases; replay checkouts expose ancestor Git history; the replay prompt says 45 minutes while the arms enforce 20, and only the session-budget arms state the real limit; W1 arm digests were stripped-text hashes, and raw-blob hashes are now in the recon provenance report; drift and rerun status; deltas inside the spread are not claimed). Every number must come from compare-final.json, W2-decisions.md or the advisor grades. Update the summary and updated date of site/series/local-worker/index.md and site/index.md; update docs/roadmap.md (status line and W2 row: done, with the headline numbers and a link to the page), and README.md if it states W2 status. Run `python3 bench/check_site.py` and `python3 tools/check_site.py`.
items.acceptance: site/series/local-worker/worker-harness.md exists with valid front matter and a summary of at most 200 words. Its results and failure-mode tables match compare-final.json exactly (each arm row is checked). The beyond-spread column matches the beyond_spread flags. Advisor counts match advisor_grades.jsonl. The not-tested and caveats sections cover every item listed in the instructions. The local-worker series index, site/index.md and docs/roadmap.md are updated, and their updated dates are >= the page's. `python3 bench/check_site.py` and `python3 tools/check_site.py` both exit 0. No change under autopilot/.
